title: Starlink 17-36 Lifts Off from Vandenberg — B1093 13th Flight; 606th Booster Landing on OCISLY
detail: SpaceX launched 24 Starlink Group 17-36 satellites on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 7:42:49 PM PDT on April 29 (02:42 UTC April 30, 2026). Booster B1093 flew its 13th mission, landing approximately 8 minutes after liftoff on drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' (OCISLY) in the Pacific Ocean — the 194th landing on that vessel and SpaceX's 606th cumulative booster recovery overall. This was the 42nd dedicated Starlink mission of 2026 and SpaceX's 53rd orbital flight of the year. The 24 satellites were deployed to low Earth orbit as part of the Starlink Group 17 shell, expanding the constellation's polar coverage capacity. As of April 30, the Starlink constellation stands at 11,900+ total launched and approximately 10,321 in orbit (10,305 working), providing broadband service to over 10 million subscribers across 160 countries.

media.caption: Falcon 9 with Starlink Group 17-36 launches from Vandenberg SFB on April 29/30, 2026 — SpaceX's 53rd orbital mission of 2026 and the 606th booster landing

title: Motley Fool Warns of 'Historical Triple Whammy' Ahead of SpaceX IPO — June 18–30 Nasdaq Debut Targeted at $1.75T Valuation
detail: On April 30, 2026, The Motley Fool published a high-profile investor warning identifying three historical risk patterns facing SpaceX's planned June IPO: (1) major IPOs including Facebook, Alibaba, GM, UPS, and Saudi Aramco historically declined 8-38% in their first six months post-debut; (2) SpaceX's estimated price-to-sales ratio at a $1.75 trillion valuation would reach 'high double digits or low triple digits' based on projected $15-16 billion in annual revenues — a level historically associated with speculative overvaluation; and (3) bubble-bursting events have preceded and followed every major technology investment wave over the past 30+ years. The article joins a growing body of institutional due diligence ahead of SpaceX's planned June 18-30 Nasdaq debut, where the company seeks to raise $75 billion — the largest US IPO in history. SpaceX is offering an unusual 30% retail tranche (vs. the standard ~10%), broadening access for individual investors. The public S-1 is expected around May 15-22, with a management roadshow the week of June 8 and IPO pricing between June 18-30. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs are leading underwriters among 21 banks.
